title: Type a message and read the answer
what: You type a question and Jarvis answers in the box.
where: Press Alt+Space for the Jarvis bar (or click the tray icon), type in the box, press Enter.
asks: No card to just talk.
limit: The answer comes from a model running on your own PC, so a long answer can take a while.

title: Check a prompt before you send it
what: Press Coach this beside the box you type in and Jarvis reads what you wrote - not to answer it, but to say what is missing: a score, up to four gaps with the smallest fix for each, questions it would have to ask, and one rewritten version of your request.
where: Settings, Prompt coach, to turn it on. Then the Coach this button appears in the Jarvis bar on the PC and on the phone. Read the advice, then press Send mine, Send the suggestion, or Add this beside one fix to put that one clarification after your own words.
asks: No card, either way. Turning it on and turning it off both happen at once, because it reads words the chat is about to send to the same model on your own PC anyway, takes no action, and opens no way out of the PC.
limit: It never sends anything by itself, and it never REPLACES your words unless you pick the rewritten one - Add this only adds a clarification after what you wrote. A low score does not stop you sending what you wrote. It runs on the small model on this PC, so its advice is sometimes wrong and it misses things a bigger model would catch.

title: The talk button
what: You hold a button, speak, and let go.
where: On the PC, hold the talk button in the Jarvis bar. On the phone, the talk button on Home - hold it, or tap it to talk and stop at a pause.
asks: No card. What you said is checked as your voice on the PC first.
limit: The phone needs your voice trained, and the PC able to turn speech into words.

title: Say "Hey Jarvis"
what: You start talking without touching anything.
where: Turn it on in Settings, Voice, then tap Listen on the phone.
asks: Turning it on raises one approval card on the PC. Turning it off is instant.
limit: Off until you turn it on. The check cannot tell a recording or a copy of your voice from the real one, and the app says so.

title: Jarvis reads its answers aloud
what: Jarvis reads its answers aloud, in the voice you chose; a finished answer can be read out again from its own speaker button.
where: On by default: a question asked by voice gets a spoken answer, and no switch turns that off. Settings, Voice, "Answers that use what Jarvis remembers" and "Answers that use sensitive saved facts" choose whether those answers are read aloud or kept on screen. Settings, HUD, "Read-aloud buttons on answers" adds the speaker to each finished answer - it does not turn read-aloud on or off.
asks: No card to read aloud; an answer that used a sensitive fact stays on screen unless you allow it in Settings.
limit: An answer that used a sensitive saved fact stays on screen instead, unless you allow it.

title: Short answers to spoken questions
what: How spoken answers are phrased: short, natural and without markdown.
where: It happens on its own for anything you ask by voice.
asks: No card: the spoken style changes wording only, never what Jarvis does.
limit: Typed questions are unchanged, and a spoken answer can still be long if you ask for more.

title: Teach Jarvis your voice
what: Jarvis learns what you sound like, so it only listens to you.
where: Phone: Platform checks, Train my voice. Read the twelve short sentences and send them.
asks: One approval card before your voice is learned. The recordings are deleted either way.
limit: Nothing is learned until you approve it.

title: How strict the voice check is
what: You choose whether a voice turn is trusted like the talk button or asks more of you.
where: Settings, Voice, Voice check.
asks: A stricter choice is instant; a looser one raises an approval card.
limit: It cannot tell a recording or a copy from your real voice.

title: The voice Jarvis speaks with
what: You pick Jarvis's voice, hear a sample of it, and can add voices of your own.
where: Settings, Jarvis's voice. On the phone, Voice, then the Jarvis's voice row.
asks: Adding a custom voice raises a card; going back to the built-in voice is instant.
limit: The voice pack is a 350 MB download on the PC, checksum-pinned.

title: How Jarvis talks
what: On the PC, ten built-in personalities decide how Jarvis sounds - Warm Collaborator, Classic British Butler, Dry & Deadpan, Patient Advocate, Reflective Coach and five more - with four dials for humour, answer length, formality and how it addresses you. "My personalities" saves up to 20 mixes of your own, and each chat can have its own.
where: Settings, How Jarvis talks.
asks: No card either way - it changes wording only.
limit: A personality changes how Jarvis sounds, never what it does, asks or remembers, and humour never appears on a card, an error or a serious topic.

title: Write like me
what: Teach Jarvis how you write - your sentence length, contractions, greetings, words you never use, and examples of your own messages and emails - so drafts sound like you instead of a chatbot.
where: Settings, How Jarvis talks, Write like me - answer the short writing prompts, paste a sample of your own writing, or edit a draft Jarvis wrote.
asks: No card to add your own writing samples on this PC. Forgetting a sample or learned rule asks 'are you sure?' first.
limit: Names, dates, amounts, links and numbers are stripped out ([name], [date], [amount]) before a sample is kept. Using your writing style marks the turn private (style_exemplars), so it always runs on your own PC's model and never goes to a cloud service.

title: Anti-Slop filter
what: Watches what Jarvis writes for the tells that make it read as machine-made: em-dashes in prose, AI buzzwords like seamless and revolutionary, decorative comment banners in code, dead buttons and unreadable contrast. The rules are distilled from the MIT-licensed miqdadbadjuber/anti-slop ruleset, which is vendored on this PC - nothing is downloaded when it runs.
where: Settings, How Jarvis talks, Anti-Slop filter. On the phone, Settings, How Jarvis talks, which has the switch, the em-dash exemption and the During/After mode.
asks: No card either way - it changes only how an answer is worded.
limit: Off costs 0 prompt tokens: nothing is added to a prompt and no answer is rewritten. The rules really checked in code are a fixed list (em-dashes, buzzwords, comment banners, dead buttons, contrast, focus rings, glass and glow caps); layout, taste and rendered sizes are guidance only, and the Playwright suites are what prove those. The three scopes, the Delivery Gate switch and the three Liveliness dials are on the desktop card only; the phone has the switch, the em-dash exemption and the mode. Allow em-dashes is off by default, and Write Like Me's own em-dash habit already wins whether it is on or off.

title: Interrupt Jarvis while it talks
what: You can cut in by talking, instead of waiting for the answer to finish.
where: Settings, Voice - the one interrupt setting: by voice, by tap only, or not at all.
asks: No card.
limit: About two seconds of what you say is checked for your voice only, and is never written down.

title: Jarvis Live
what: A back-and-forth voice conversation you start and stop, with no wake word between turns.
where: Press Start Live in the Jarvis bar, or say "Hey Jarvis, let's talk". On the phone, Live on Home or the Quick Settings tile. A PC hotkey can start and end it (asked for once, off until you pick one).
asks: Cards are still decided by tapping, never by voice. Ending Live never asks.
limit: Not full-duplex, so a turn takes a couple of seconds. The voice check still runs on every clip, and side remarks meant for someone else are ignored and not kept.

title: The extras around Live
what: A phone tile, a headset button, and a "Live ended - Resume" note.
where: Phone: the Quick Settings tile, or a headset button - press stops Jarvis talking, a long press mutes the microphone.
asks: The headset button never approves anything.
limit: Live pauses itself during a phone or video call, where the phone can tell one is happening.

title: Talk-to-type
what: You hold a key, speak, and Jarvis types what you said into the program in front.
where: Hold Alt+Shift+T (changeable in Settings, Shortcuts). A quick tap keeps it listening until you press it again.
asks: One approval card to switch it on; after that no card each time. Switching it off is instant.
limit: On the PC only - a client must not turn speech into words. It waits while Jarvis Live is on.
surface_reason: The PC types what you say into the program in front, using a key you hold there; a phone must not turn speech into words, so it has no such key to hold (the row's own limit).

title: The whole conversation, and carrying it on
what: The current chat is one scrollable thread, and an earlier chat can be picked up again. Under an answer, a quiet line says how many saved facts it used, and pressing it shows them.
where: Scroll the Jarvis bar (or Home on the phone). History has "Continue this chat" and an "Earlier chats" link. How long a chat can sit before the next message starts a new one is in Settings, A new conversation starts after.
asks: No card.
limit: The thread hides while "Hide memory lists and chat history" is on. A new conversation starts after 30 quiet minutes by default - 10 minutes, 1 hour, 4 hours or never can be chosen in Settings - and the old one stays in History, where Continue brings it back.

title: Incognito chat
what: A chat where nothing is kept and nothing you have saved is used.
where: Incognito chat in the Jarvis bar. Games and role-play use it automatically.
asks: No card.
limit: Only on a PC that has it. It also learns nothing from what you say there - no fact is saved, even with a "Remember:".

title: Private chat
what: A chat where Jarvis answers from the model alone: it searches nothing - not the web, your history or your files - uses none of your saved memory, keeps nothing and learns nothing, and cannot change a setting, save an item or run an action.
where: The Private chip beside Incognito in the Jarvis bar. Turning it on or off starts a new conversation, so a private chat and a normal one never mix.
asks: No card for turning it on, and none from it: nothing it does would need a card.
limit: It only works on a PC whose version of Jarvis has it: an older PC leaves it off and says why instead of quietly sending an ordinary chat. It cannot be on at the same time as Incognito - turning one on turns the other off. The phone has no Private chip on purpose: its private mode is Incognito, which is not the same guarantee - Incognito can still run tools.
surface_reason: The phone has no Private chip on purpose: its private mode is Incognito, which is not the same guarantee, because Incognito can still run tools (the row's own limit).

title: Search what was said
what: A search box for your own past chats.
where: History, the search box.
asks: No card - it is shown on screen only, and never handed to the AI.
limit: Hidden while the private lists are hidden.

title: The morning briefing
what: A short brief with your calendar, your new email and the weather.
where: Set it up in Settings, Morning briefing. The latest one is in Brain, Work, Morning briefing.
asks: Setting one up repeats, so it raises one card. "Brief me now" raises none.
limit: Shows the count and the senders of new email unless you choose the count only.

title: Timers, alarms, reminders and lists
what: Jarvis keeps your timers, alarms, reminders, to-do lists and the standby schedule on this PC, and shows them to the phone too.
where: Just ask - "remind me at six", "remind me in 30 minutes to check my phone", "make a reminder for 30 minutes from now", "set a timer for 10 minutes" - or see them in Brain, Work, Coming up and the HUD's Reminders panel (#rail-reminders).
asks: A plain timer, a one-time reminder, a repeating reminder, an alarm and the standby schedule need no card. The morning briefing and "tell me when" raise one.
limit: The PC is the clock. When one goes off, while Jarvis is running on the PC it shows a Windows notification: an alarm keeps ringing, a reminder or timer shows once. With the Jarvis app fully closed no notification appears then, but the job is kept and shows when it opens; a late alarm rings only if at most 10 minutes late, after that it is a quiet missed note. While the phone is connected to the PC the same job also shows an Android notification; the phone sets no alarm of its own. The morning briefing and "tell me when" raise one approval card.

title: Today
what: Your own cards for the day in one place, gathered from the lists the PC already keeps.
where: Brain, Work, Today.
asks: No card; adding one is held while the connection is catching up.
limit: It only gathers cards the PC's own lists already hold; a card added while the connection catches up follows that card's own rule.

title: Widgets you describe
what: Small tiles you asked for, drawn on your desktop widget or your phone's home screen, in one of four arrangements.
where: Brain, Work, Widgets (desktop); Brain, Widgets and a home-screen slot (phone). The desktop widget itself shows with Alt+Shift+W.
asks: No card.
limit: A widget's tile actions are a fixed set, its arrangement is one of four fixed ones, and nothing a widget shows is ever turned into an instruction.

title: Background jobs
what: The long jobs Jarvis is running, whether they finished, and the one button that stops a running one.
where: Brain, Work, Background jobs.
asks: No card to look; stopping one never asks.
limit: Only jobs the PC itself started; closing the list does not stop one, and stopping a running job never asks.

title: What Jarvis is doing right now
what: The state Jarvis is in, each step it is taking, and anything it noticed by itself, from the PC's own modules.
where: Brain, Now.
asks: No card.
limit: Only what the PC's own modules report; it does not predict what will happen next.

title: How much Jarvis may interrupt you
what: The interruption budget, and the day's brief of what needs you.
where: Brain, Now, Attention budget. The brief appears in the Jarvis bar.
asks: Muting is instant, and approves nothing.
limit: The budget can mute interruptions; it approves nothing and cannot make Jarvis act.

title: Focus session
what: A timer plus Quiet, with Jarvis naming a distraction out loud and a report at the end.
where: Brain, Work, Focus session. Snooze, "I'm doing research", pause and stop by voice.
asks: No card - it is off unless you start it.
limit: It watches which app is in front on the PC only, and keeps counts, never what it saw. The report has no streak line.

title: Play or pause what is on this PC
what: Pause, play, skip to the next or previous song or video, and ask what is playing.
where: Say the object with the action - "pause the music", "next song", "what's playing". Bare "pause" while a focus session is running is the focus session's; it controls the media session already playing on the PC.
asks: No card: it controls only the player that is already playing on this PC.
limit: It can only control a media session Windows reports; a player Windows does not expose, or a hidden tab, is not touched.

title: The Memory tab
what: One place for everything Jarvis knows and how it learns.
where: Brain, Memory.
asks: No card.
limit: The lists hide while "Hide memory lists and chat history" is on.

title: Facts Jarvis saved by itself
what: Everyday things about you and your projects, saved without asking each time.
where: Brain, Memory, Saved automatically. The switch that governs it is also in Settings, Learning.
asks: Everyday facts save with no card. Health, money, passwords and account numbers wait for your yes.
limit: Only your own words count - never a web page, an email, a document or tool output.

title: Facts waiting for your yes
what: Facts Jarvis wants to keep, held until you answer.
where: Brain, Memory, Waiting for you - or the card that appears.
asks: One card per fact, or one card covering several; nothing is saved until you answer.
limit: This is the one list that is never hidden.

title: What Jarvis knows about you
what: The facts, by topic, each with Forget and Erase the words.
where: Brain, Memory, What Jarvis knows about you.
asks: Forget asks "are you sure?" first. Erase the words asks too, and cannot be undone - only the dates stay.
limit: Erasing a fact's words can also offer to delete the chat it came from.
surface_reason: The full list of what Jarvis knows, with Forget and Erase the words, is the PC's own Memory page; the phone shows its saved and waiting facts, not this list.

title: People and things
what: The people and things your facts are linked to.
where: Brain, Memory, People and things.
asks: No card to look. Forget on a fact asks first, as it does anywhere.
limit: The desktop keeps no people-and-things list of its own.
surface_reason: The desktop has no people-and-things list of its own: the list is a read-only phone view of names the facts already name, while joining two entries, the names under each fact, "About <name>" and the merge card stay the desktop's (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 8).

title: Person dossier
what: One person's dossier: what Jarvis already knows about them, the kept chats and mail that name them, the open to-dos and the next shared event, all read-only.
where: Brain, Memory, People and things - click (or tap) a person's name.
asks: No card: it only reads. Nothing is changed by opening a dossier.
limit: Opens a person's dossier from People and things on both apps; while App lock or hidden lists are on it shows nothing but one sentence.

title: Always keep in mind
what: Facts put into every answer.
where: Brain, Memory, Always keep in mind.
asks: Pinning one fact is one tap, with no question. Unpinning is instant.
limit: It holds a fixed number of characters, and the card says how many are used.

title: Between us
what: Inside jokes and shared references, from your own words only, kept with your memory.
where: Brain, Memory, Between us.
asks: Forget asks first, like any other fact.
limit: Only from your own words; shared references are memory-like and hide with the memory lists.

title: Topics
what: A mode for each topic of what Jarvis learns.
where: Brain, Memory, Topics.
asks: The PC raises the only cards here; every change is held while the connection is catching up.
limit: A topic changes what Jarvis learns; the PC raises the cards and every change waits while the connection catches up.

title: The learning switches
what: Whether Jarvis learns by itself, and how much it remembers.
where: Brain, Memory, Learning. The two switches are also in Settings, Learning.
asks: Turning automatic learning on raises a card; turning it off is instant. "Also remember sensitive topics automatically" is off by default.
limit: Everyday facts are learned automatically by default.

title: The wiki Jarvis builds
what: A wiki built from documents you give Jarvis, with pages it keeps up to date as you add more.
where: Brain, Memory, Wiki.
asks: Adding a document raises one card.
limit: Built only from documents you give it; it does not read the web on its own.

title: Deep questions
what: Slow, deeper questions and the answers they produced.
where: Brain, Memory, Deep questions.
asks: No card per question - the switch was approved once. Asking is held while the connection is catching up.
limit: The questions and answers are your own words, so they hide with the memory lists.

title: What did I believe on this date?
what: Ask what a fact said on a past day and see the answer it gave before.
where: Brain, Memory, What did I believe on this date?
asks: No card.
limit: It needs the connection live.

title: Bring in old chats
what: Import a chat export from ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or DeepSeek.
where: Brain, Memory, Bring in old chats.
asks: It only proposes: every fact it finds waits for its own yes.
limit: Imported text is outside text - it is never learned from.

title: Your past chats
what: The chats Jarvis kept, with the switches that govern keeping them.
where: Brain, History. In the HUD, the History button in the left column. On the phone, the History row in the Brain.
asks: Turning keeping back on raises a card; deleting one chat is instant; forgetting what a chat taught asks first.
limit: Kept on the PC, encrypted, by default. This phone keeps none of it.

title: Chat tags
what: Tag your chats yourself, and let Jarvis suggest tags overnight.
where: Brain, History, Chat tags.
asks: Tagging a chat yourself needs no card. Turning the overnight suggestions on raises one card, and every tag it suggests is one more - a suggestion is filed only if you tap it.
limit: Tags hide with the private lists.

title: Forget a time frame
what: Forget what Jarvis learned or said over a stretch of days.
where: Brain, History, Forget a time frame.
asks: One card listing every item, decided by tapping only - never by voice. Then 10 minutes to Undo.
limit: After the 10 minutes the chats are gone for good. Erasing a fact's words for good stays the separate per-fact action.

title: Galaxy
what: A map of what Jarvis knows, drawn from your own facts. On the desktop it opens on the Planetary Orrery, and you can pick any of eight looks from the Look menu beside the lenses: Planetary orbit, Neural arbor, Nebula, DNA helix, Radar dome, Star map, Clean tree and Zen ring. The choice is remembered on this PC. On a PC that can draw 3D the eight look like the demo page they came from - a real starfield, fog, and the guide shapes each look is built around - and each look has two small buttons of its own. On the phone it is a read-only picture: at most 48 names, no labels, and a tap opens that name's facts.
where: Brain, Galaxy (desktop). Brain, Memory, People and things (phone).
asks: No card.
limit: Drawn from the same memory lists, so it hides with them. On a PC that cannot draw 3D - or with reduced motion on - each look is drawn flat instead, in the same shapes. Three of the looks would like details the PC does not send (a saved thing's topic, its date and its safety ring), so the Nebula, DNA helix and Radar dome work those out from what kind of thing each name is; the Radar dome's three rings are kinds of thing, not a claim about safety. The phone's picture is read-only - no add, edit, merge or drag - and the names it leaves out stay in the list below.

title: Read the words in a recording or video
what: Ask Jarvis to read one audio or video file from a folder it may look in. It transcribes the speech on this PC, with timestamps, and reads the on-screen text in a few sampled video frames. It returns a transcript, never a summary. A separate switch, on by default, keeps the words searchable as readable text on this PC until you delete them - spoken words and, for a video, on-screen words from up to eight sampled frames.
where: Either app's chat: name the file, for example `read the words in C:\Users\you\Videos\talk.mp4`. The file and all the reading are on the PC; the answer is written by the local model.
asks: No card of its own for a read: a file already inside a folder you allow is the same read_files_readonly rule as my_files, and the result is treated as outside text. The separate searchable-recordings switch decides whether readable words are kept; nothing is ever sent anywhere.
limit: English speech only; one file of at most 10 minutes and 100 MB; a WAV needs nothing else, other formats need ffmpeg installed on the PC (a missing ffmpeg is a plain refusal). It does not understand the picture in a video and cannot label speakers. The words are never learned as a fact; the optional searchable index keeps readable text on this PC until you delete it.

title: Where did I put things
what: Remember where you put something from your own words - "the spare key is under the blue pot" - and answer "where did I put the key?".
where: Just tell Jarvis where something is, then ask where you put it; both are your own words.
asks: No card for an ordinary place; a sensitive place - a spare key, a home-security detail - waits for your yes, like any sensitive fact.
limit: Only what you told it in your own words; it does not look through the house or the files, and forgetting it is Memory's own Forget.

title: Look at this
what: Jarvis looks at the window in front of you, once, and answers about it - and hands you the cleaned picture of that look, so you can ask about a chart or an error message.
where: Press Alt+Shift+S on the PC, or say "look at this". On the phone, the assistant gesture. The picture waits in the question box.
asks: No card. The picture is never saved; the question and the answer are kept like any other chat.
limit: Passwords, keys and card numbers are painted solid black first, and if Jarvis's own window is in front - or the cleaner cannot check the picture - none is attached and Jarvis says why. With one graphics card it reads the screen's words; picture mode can read the picture too, slowly, and is off by default.

title: Watch with me
what: A live look at your screen that you start and stop.
where: Settings, Look at this and Watch with me, or the Watch button in the Jarvis bar. A key can be picked for it (Alt+Shift+V is free).
asks: Starting is held while the connection is catching up or App lock would ask; stopping never is.
limit: A visible "Jarvis is watching" sign shows the whole time. It pauses on password fields and on the apps you exclude (banking), and nothing is saved.

title: Picture mode
what: Let the PC read the picture of your screen, not only its words.
where: Settings, Look at this and Watch with me, Picture mode.
asks: Turning it on raises one card on the PC; turning it off is instant.
limit: Off by default, slow, and it runs on the processor rather than the graphics card.

title: Photo to reminder
what: Show Jarvis a photo of a letter or an appointment card and it offers the dates it can read.
where: Share the picture into Jarvis from the phone, or paste it in the Jarvis bar.
asks: It only proposes. Your tap adds ONE reminder, with no card.
limit: The dates are read on the PC, and a scan sets nothing up by itself.

title: Show Jarvis the camera in Live
what: During a Live session you can show Jarvis what the phone's camera sees.
where: Nothing to press yet - inside Jarvis Live the phone says showing it from the phone comes in a later update.
asks: No extra card - the Live session is already running.
limit: Off until the photo test passes on the 12 GB card - the card is installed, but this feature is not measured. There is no words-only camera on one card.
surface_reason: The phone's camera only: a PC webcam mostly sees the owner's face and room (the owner's answers of 2026-09-28, docs/LIVE-DESIGN.md section 5; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 8).

title: Quiz me on a text
what: Jarvis writes questions on something you paste, or on a YouTube video.
where: Brain, Work, Quiz me on a text.
asks: No card, and nothing is saved.
limit: A YouTube quiz sends the link once (one card) and keeps it nowhere.

title: Ask for a picture, and keep it
what: You type what the picture should show, and Jarvis draws it on your PC and keeps it, with a note beside it saying what made it. Both apps show the ones you kept, and the phone can save one to itself.
where: PC: Brain, Projects, Pictures. Phone: Brain, Pictures.
asks: No card. A picture is a new file in a folder on your PC, drawn by a program on your PC, from your own words - the same as a timer or a note. A draw may first stop and ask, in plain words, whether Jarvis may set the everyday chat aside for about seven minutes; sending the same request again is your yes, from either app.
limit: Nothing is ever sent anywhere: there is no share, no upload and no email. The feature starts switched off (Settings, Pictures, "Making pictures") because it shares the second graphics card with the everyday model, and it needs ComfyUI or stable-diffusion.cpp installed on the PC first. The pictures and their prompts hide while "Hide memory lists and chat history" is on.

title: Search what was said in audio and video
what: Keep the words it reads from recordings and videos in a searchable index on this PC, so they can be searched later.
where: Settings, Searchable recordings and videos (the media index); it only looks inside folders already listed for Jarvis.
asks: It is on by default - your decision of 2026-10-19. Turning it off is instant, and turning it back on raises one card.
limit: Only folders already listed; it stores readable words on this PC, never the audio or video itself, and the words are never learned as a fact. Delete removes the stored words for good.
surface_reason: The index lives on this PC and has a PC Settings card; the phone has no recordings-index screen.

title: My study decks
what: Questions you kept, asked again on a schedule the PC works out from your answers.
where: Brain, Work, My study decks.
asks: No card.
limit: The words hide with the private lists.

title: Write a note for you
what: Jarvis writes a note into Obsidian, Logseq or Joplin.
where: Say "note this" in chat (2026-10-31) or press Alt+Shift+N (one of the PC's changeable shortcuts in Settings, Shortcuts) to open the bar ready to file one. The notes editor's own Ctrl+B and friends work inside the editor.
asks: No card normally. In a turn where Jarvis has read an email, a page or a file, writing a note raises one.
limit: Only the note apps this PC is set up for. The quick-note key opens the bar ready to file; it does not save by itself, and the phone has no keyboard shortcuts. With App lock on, adding a note to a running task needs an unlock first.

title: Create and customize your notes
what: Browse, search, create, extend, surgically change, rename and move notes in your Obsidian vault from the PC or the phone, and use the PC editor's formatting toolbar and templates.
where: The PC's Brain → Memory → Notes; the phone's Brain → What Jarvis knows about you → Notes. The create, customize, rename and move sentences work in chat on either app.
asks: Reading and searching ask nothing. Creating a note, adding to it, changing one line, renaming or moving it, or saving a template raises ONE approval card; denying it changes nothing.
limit: Obsidian vault only, one note per request; no deleting a note or a line, no bulk edits, no moving outside the vault, no folder renames and no cloud sync. A note change waits while the turn has read outside text.

title: Folders Jarvis may look in
what: The folders Jarvis is allowed to read, and the Notion export.
where: Settings, Folders Jarvis may look in.
asks: Adding a folder goes through the Windows picker and raises one card; removing one is instant.
limit: A Notion export goes into a folder Jarvis searches; imported notes are outside text and are never learned as facts.

title: Ask about a PDF, a Word file or a Notion page
what: Jarvis reads a document you point it at and answers questions about it.
where: Put the file in a folder Jarvis may look in, then ask about it.
asks: Reading needs no card. Writing a note back after reading it raises one, as any note write after outside text does.
limit: Only files in a folder Jarvis may look in; text from a document is outside text and is never learned as a fact.

title: Tutorials and the FAQ
what: Step-by-step tutorials with your place kept, and the usual questions answered.

title: Cloud (DeepSeek API)
what: Send a hard question to the one cloud API service you chose - DeepSeek by default - after your yes, or let the standing switch send one without asking each time. The Cloud preset chooses the service; it does not switch the answer by itself.
where: PC: Settings, Presets, the Cloud row, then pick a provider whose key is saved. The per-question Try the cloud model button is under an offered answer in either app; the standing switch is in the same Cloud row. On the phone the Cloud state is readable but choosing and switching are the PC's.
asks: Applying the Cloud row raises ONE change_own_config card; so does turning the standing switch on. Turning it off is instant. Every privacy gate still runs first, and the monthly money limit still applies.
limit: One cloud service at a time. Its key lives in Windows Credential Manager (presence only is shown, never the key or a fragment), is never logged or echoed, and goes only to that service's own host. No key, no monthly limit or no usable model means no cloud turn. Email, files, credentials, stored memory, a picture, your screen, a private question or a tainted conversation never go. The newest message's own words are what is sent, not the earlier conversation. A chat answer is from the local model unless a cloud turn was allowed; the UI says so on the card.

title: The second graphics card
what: The switches that put extra work on the second card, and which card everyday chat runs on.
where: Settings, Second graphics card.
asks: Turning a switch on raises one card; turning it off is instant. Pinning everyday chat raises its own card.
limit: The card is installed, but its features are not measured - every switch stays off until you turn it on.

title: The big model (slow)
what: One bigger model split across both cards, for the hardest questions.
where: Settings, Big model (slow).
asks: Turning a switch on raises one card; turning it off is instant.
limit: Slow, and only worth it with both cards installed.

title: Updates
what: Whether a newer build of this app exists, and installing it.
where: Settings, Updates. On the phone it is "Check for new versions" on Platform checks, under This app. Each app checks its own release page.
asks: Nothing installs by itself - you press to install, then to restart.
limit: Each app checks its own release page; installing never starts by itself, and a version it cannot read is said plainly.

title: Check for tool updates
what: Reports the packages and tools on this PC that are out of date.
where: Settings, Check for tool updates.
asks: Asks the first time only, then never again. Turning it off is instant.
limit: Updating a tool is a change, and raises its own card first.
surface_reason: It reports the packages and tools installed on this PC, and a phone has no such package list to check.

title: The settings file, the logs and starting with Windows
what: The folded card at the end of Settings: start Jarvis with Windows, the log folder, the crash notes.
where: Settings, More options.
asks: Starting with Windows is one tap; the log folder only opens a folder.
limit: Starting with Windows is one login setting; the logs and crash notes open folders, they never upload.
surface_reason: The settings file, the log folder and starting with Windows are the PC's own files and startup, and the phone has none of them.

title: What this backend supports
what: The list of abilities the app checks before offering a button.
where: Settings, What this backend supports.
asks: No card - it only reads.
limit: It lists the names only, never their values.

title: About Jarvis
what: The version, the licences and the credits, with nothing to change.
where: Settings, About Jarvis. On the phone it is the end of Help.
asks: No card.
limit: Only reads the version, licences and credits; it changes nothing.

title: The big HUD window
what: The larger always-there window, with its own chat box.
where: Tray menu, Show the HUD window. Its box opens the Jarvis bar for anything more.
asks: No card.
limit: The HUD's own chat box has no Incognito chat, no New conversation and no crisis panel.
surface_reason: A phone has no HUD window: the big always-there panel is a PC surface (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 8).

title: Backups
what: One locked backup file, into a folder you pick. Your phone reads what is in that folder and can ask the PC to make a new one.
where: Settings, Backups. On the phone too, in Settings.
asks: Setting the folder raises one card. Restoring is one card that always needs Windows Hello. Asking for a backup from the phone raises nothing: the file is written only once you say you have saved the recovery code the phone shows you.
limit: Locked with a recovery code only you have, shown once - lose the code and the backup is useless, and Jarvis cannot recover it. The phone shows the code and will not write the file until you tick that you have saved it, so an unfinished run leaves your PC untouched. Jarvis cannot prove from the phone that a backup opens: only the code opens one, and codes are only typed on the PC. Each new backup deletes the oldest of the last few kept, so making many pushes older copies out. Erased facts stay in older backups until they age out.

title: Accounts and keys
what: The mail password, the private calendar link and the Home Assistant token, kept on this PC.
where: Settings, Accounts.
asks: Saving a secret writes it straight into Windows Credential Manager - never over HTTP, never shown again.
limit: The phone is never asked for an account secret.
surface_reason: The phone is never asked for an account secret: the mail password, the calendar link and the Home Assistant token are kept on the PC (the row's own limit).

title: What Jarvis can reach
what: Every way Jarvis can reach something outside itself, and whether it is on right now.
where: Settings, What Jarvis can reach.
asks: No card - it only reads the PC's own settings and the live state of each way out.
limit: Read-only, and it changes nothing. Which tools can be switched on from Settings, What asks first is decided there; raw shell, computer and browser control, web-page reading, account connection and REA stay settings-file choices.

title: Undo
what: The changes you can still undo.
where: Brain, Work, Undo shelf. On the phone it is the shelf on the Inbox.
asks: Undo itself never asks.
limit: Some things offer 10 minutes to undo; after that they are gone.

title: Activity: cards you already decided
what: A read-only list of past approvals.
where: Brain, Work, Activity. On the phone it is its own Past approvals screen, opened from the Inbox.
asks: No card - it only reads.
limit: It shows the title, Approved / Denied / Timed out, when, and which device.

title: Limits and frequency
what: The numbers Jarvis keeps to: how long you can undo, how much it gets on with at once, what counts as news from a project you watch, how many cards a study run shows, how long a chat must sit before the overnight tag suggester may read it, and whether a model looks for people and things in what you save.
where: Settings, Limits and frequency - on the PC and on the phone.
asks: Turning a number down changes at once. Turning one up that lets Jarvis do more is a loosening, so the PC puts one approval card to you first and writes nothing until you answer.
limit: Only what the PC's own table offers: every limit names a setting the PC already reads, and the phone may not change the ones the table marks for the PC alone.

title: Change a setting by asking, in any words
what: You say what you want changed - "turn off quiet hours", "stop showing me notifications on my watch" - and Jarvis changes that switch, in whatever words you use. You do not have to remember one particular phrase.
where: Ask in the Jarvis bar on the PC, or by voice or by typing on the phone. Ask "what can I change?" and Jarvis lists every switch it can reach this way.
asks: Only a change that loosens a rule, or turns on something that reads or reaches more: that raises ONE approval card - Windows Hello where that setting already asks for it - and nothing changes until you answer it. A cosmetic change (the prompt coach, humour, the voice following the face, making pictures, this PC's own notification switches) happens at once, with no card.
limit: It changes Jarvis's own switches and nothing else - never a file, a folder, a key or anything outside. A switch it has no way to reach (App lock, the Windows Hello memory-list switch, the theme, the floating face, starting with Windows) is answered in words that say where to change it by hand: nothing is changed and no card is raised. A turn shaped by a web page, an email or a file Jarvis read changes nothing at all, so a page cannot talk it into a setting change. It is on out of the box (the owner's decision of 2026-10-13) - to take it back off, drop "change_setting" from the tool list in the settings file; see backend/README.md.

title: Start the local model when it is not running
what: When Jarvis can answer but its local model server is not running, both apps draw a standing line saying so - and now offer ONE button on it, "Start the local model". The button does not start a program of its own: it asks the PC to run the owner's OWN Windows logon task for the lane the chat uses, found on that PC by the half of its name a rename does not touch. Then it watches that lane until it really answers, and says so.
where: PC: the Jarvis bar's notice under the input, and the widget's model row. Phone: the status line at the top of Home. Both show the button only while the lane is down AND the PC says a press would really start something.
asks: No card. It runs the same task the owner's own logon already runs unattended, so a card would only be stricter than the thing it duplicates; pressing the button is itself the owner's explicit act. One lane, the one Jarvis talks to - never both.
limit: Only the lane the chat is pointed at, and only when this PC has such a task. Starting a task is not the model arriving: the line is cleared only when the lane actually answers, and a start that does not come up says so and leaves the warning standing.

title: Jarvis starts the local model again by itself when it dies
what: When the local model server stops answering, Jarvis itself starts it again - on the PC, in the background, with nobody pressing anything. It runs the SAME one action the button above runs: the owner's own Windows logon task for the lane the chat uses. It looks every 30 seconds, the look is one small question to the lane on this PC (no model call, nothing spent), and when the lane is back both apps say so in plain words: "Jarvis started the local model again at 08:19, because it was not running."
where: Nothing to press: the line appears by itself in the Jarvis bar and the widget on the PC, and on Home's status line on the phone. It carries one button, "Don't restart it for me", which turns the automatic restarting off at once - and "Restart it automatically again" while it is off.
asks: No card, in either direction. It runs the same task the owner's own logon already runs unattended, so a card would only be stricter than the thing it duplicates; turning it back on is the same action the Start button beside it takes in the same second. The owner asked for it in these words on 2026-10-14: "Also restart the lane automatically when it dies."
limit: Bounded, and it stops rather than hammering: a minute of being down before the first try, at most 3 tries in one episode, 5 minutes and then 10 between them, and then it gives up - only the standing warning remains, with the Start button still there. It never starts a second copy while one is starting, and never touches a lane that is answering. A lane stopped on purpose cannot be told from one that crashed: if Jarvis starts it again, it says so, and the button is how the owner says "not that one".

title: Clipboard history, and three one-press cleanups for what you copy
what: A drawer at the Jarvis bar keeps the last 25 things you copied, newest first, in this PC's memory only - and turns a copied table, a blob of JSON or a link into one press each: Table, Pretty JSON or Clean link. Password managers, one-time codes, private keys, card numbers and empty copies are never kept.
where: Press Alt+Shift+C on the PC to open it - the key only opens the drawer, and it can be changed in Settings, Shortcuts.
asks: No card. Nothing is kept until you press Turn on in the drawer, and that press is the permission.
limit: PC only: the phone's clipboard belongs to the phone's own OS and keyboard, and the drawer lives at the PC's Jarvis bar, so the phone has no clipboard history. On the PC it is off on every launch, held in memory - never written to disk, never logged - and wiped when Jarvis or Windows locks.
surface_reason: The phone's clipboard belongs to the phone's own OS and keyboard, and the drawer lives at the PC's Jarvis bar, so the phone has no clipboard history (the row's own limit).

title: File history
what: Jarvis keeps a copy of a file before it changes one, so you can see exactly what changed and put a version back.
where: Brain -> Projects -> File history. Show the difference draws the change in the module's own bounded diff; Put this version back asks first.
asks: Showing a difference asks nothing. A restore raises ONE card in the Jarvis bar; a denied or timed-out card changes nothing. The whole drawer hides while App lock or Hide memory lists and chat history is on.
limit: This PC only: the copies are files on this PC, and a phone has no page for them.
surface_reason: The copies are files on this PC, and a phone has no page for them (the row's own limit).

title: A reminder that opens something, or asks to do one task
what: One reminder can carry one action: show a note, open a web page, open a file on this PC, or ask to put the morning briefing together.
where: PC: Reminders, Then. Phone: shows a note and the one card; no way to create or edit one.
asks: Opening something asks nothing: the reminder names the whole address or file and nothing opens until you press Open. A task is one card when the reminder goes off, every time, and nothing runs without your yes.
limit: One action per reminder, and no shell, command, script, webhook or program to run: a page, a file inside a folder Jarvis may look in, a note, or the briefing. A backup is refused, because its recovery code would be shown to nobody. Opening is this PC's.
surface_reason: Creating one is the desktop HUD's alone, for now, because a file target has to be a path inside a folder the PC lists and the phone cannot read the PC's folders; opening the target is the PC's, because the file is on the PC and the page opens in the PC's browser, and the phone still shows the note and approves the one task card.
aliases: open a page from a reminder
open a file from a reminder
run a task from a reminder

title: Thinking levels
what: Choose Off, Quick, Deep or Auto thinking for the running model: how much it reasons before it answers.
where: Settings, Thinking levels; or say "think deeply", "quick answer" or "what thinking level is on?".
asks: Changes take effect at once and need no card; both apps show one row for each running model.
limit: Per running model - switching model or lane can change which level applies, and the level cannot make a model see more than its context allows.

title: Do arithmetic
what: Jarvis does arithmetic accurately instead of a language model guessing the sum.
where: Just ask a sum - "what is 18% of 240?" - the model uses the calculator tool.
asks: No card: it is arithmetic only.
limit: Only arithmetic the calculator tool supports; it does not run arbitrary code or maths that needs a library the tool does not have.

title: Open a program or Windows panel by name
what: Open a program or a Windows panel from your own words - "open Notion", "open settings", "open Jarvis settings".
where: Just say "open ..."; the app opens the program this PC's Start menu finds, or the named Windows panel.
asks: No card to open a program; opening is looked up on this PC, never guessed.
limit: Only programs this PC's Start menu finds and the Windows panels named; an ambiguous name is asked back, and nothing is typed into the program.

title: Find and grade a library on GitHub
what: Search GitHub for a coding idea, read the candidates and grade them for this project.
where: Off by default; there is no in-app switch. Add github_search by hand to the settings file (jarvis-framework.toml, [tools].enabled), then ask.
asks: Off until its line is added by hand to the settings file; reading public pages needs no card once it is offered.
limit: Off by default; public GitHub only, no private repo and no token beyond what you configured; it reads pages, it does not install anything.

title: Click and type in another program
what: Click and type in another Windows program by naming its controls.
where: Off by default; there is no in-app switch. Add control_computer by hand to the settings file (jarvis-framework.toml, [tools].enabled), then ask.
asks: Off until its line is added by hand to the settings file; each action is one approved call.
limit: Off by default; it can only use controls the accessibility tree exposes, never a hidden window, and it does not type passwords.

title: Drive one browser tab
what: Drive one browser tab by naming page elements - click, type, read the page.
where: Off by default; there is no in-app switch. Add browser_control by hand to the settings file (jarvis-framework.toml, [tools].enabled), then ask.
asks: Off until its line is added by hand to the settings file; each action is one approved call on the tab you named.
limit: Off by default; one tab, elements it can name, no other tab and no downloads.

title: Run one shell command
what: Run one shell command on this PC and return its output.
where: Off by default; there is no in-app switch. Add shell_exec by hand to the settings file (jarvis-framework.toml, [tools].enabled), then ask.
asks: Off until its line is added by hand to the settings file; one approved call per command.
limit: Off by default; one command and its own output, nothing interactive - it can change files, so keep it off unless you need it.

title: Read one web page out loud
what: Fetch the one page you named and read its words out loud.
where: Off by default; there is no in-app switch for it. Add read_web_page by hand to the settings file (jarvis-framework.toml, [tools].enabled), then ask about a page.
asks: Every read shows the exact address on its own card before anything is fetched. What comes back is outside text - never learned, never acted on.
limit: Off by default; one page, no links followed, and the page is read only as outside text.

title: Inspect a program or app statically
what: Statically inspect a program, app or binary and report what it does - strings, imports, structure.
where: Off by default; set [rea] enabled and add rea_investigate by hand in the settings file (jarvis-framework.toml), then ask.
asks: Off by default; every investigation is one approved call.
limit: Off by default; static inspection only - it does not run the program, and a packed or protected binary may tell it little.

title: Build the Android app in a project task
what: Build the Android app in a project task and install the APK over the cable - two separate approvals.
where: In a project task, ask for the Android build; Gradle runs on this PC and adb installs it over the cable. Building and installing are separate cards.
asks: Two risky cards, each with its exact command: one for the build (app_build_android) and one for the install (app_install_android).
limit: Only a project already set up for the Android app; it needs the SDK/JDK on this PC and a cable, and it never publishes to Play.

title: Docker containers Jarvis ships
what: List the Docker containers Jarvis ships (such as its own SearXNG) and start or stop one.
where: Routes only, no app page: GET /api/docker/containers and /api/docker/service. The Docker plugin ships the containers.
asks: Starting a container is the give-more direction and must ask (tier ask); stopping is the give-less direction and is instant unless your settings make it ask. Listing is free.
limit: Only the containers Jarvis itself ships; it never pulls a new image.
surface_reason: Docker runs on this PC only; the phone has no Docker screen.

title: Approval cards
what: One card for each thing Jarvis wants to do that is not completely safe.
where: The card appears in the Jarvis bar, the widget, the HUD, or on the phone's Home.
asks: Nothing runs until you decide. There is no approve-all anywhere. Approving a risky card asks for Windows Hello on the PC, or your screen lock on the phone.
limit: Four cards wait for you instead of expiring after 15 minutes - pairing a device, unretiring a shared key, registering a phone's approval key, and restoring a backup. On a PC with no Windows Hello, or a phone with no screen lock, a risky approval is refused until one is set up, with a plain message saying how.

title: What asks first
what: Every action Jarvis can take and whether it asks you first, in plain words.
where: Settings, What asks first - in both apps.
asks: A "make stricter" switch is instant. Loosening one action is PC-only and costs one card plus Windows Hello. Offering a tool to the AI model is a separate one-tool switch (Tier A/B, see the report), PC-only, with ONE card plus Windows Hello each; turning it off is instant.
limit: Tier C (raw shell, computer and browser control, reading one web page, connecting an account, REA) and the tools this slice leaves alone are not offered in-app; they stay a settings-file choice. Nothing switches two tools at once, and the phone is read-only.

title: Lock Jarvis, and hide what it remembers
what: Opening Jarvis needs your fingerprint or PIN, and the memory lists and chat history can be hidden.
where: Settings, Security.
asks: Turning a lock on is instant; turning it off, or loosening it, asks for Windows Hello or your phone's screen lock first.
limit: With App lock on, the phone blocks screenshots, and the PC's approval widget shows only a short title with Approve opening the locked app.

title: Hand a captcha to your phone ("Solve it here")
what: When Jarvis is driving a browser and hits a captcha or a sign-in page, it stops there and your phone can show a live picture of that one window so you can solve it. Jarvis never solves a captcha.
where: The phone's alert, then "Solve it here". The settings are in Settings, When the phone does not answer and When a captcha stops Jarvis - in both apps.
asks: Opening the hand-off asks nothing: your own taps and typing, on your own devices. "Keep offering it" for the full 15 minutes is one card on the PC with Windows Hello; "Stop early", the default, is instant. Leaving the stuck window exactly where it is (the default) is also instant; bringing it to the front is one card on the PC with Windows Hello.
limit: The picture is never saved and goes only to your own phone over Tailscale or NordVPN Meshnet. Some captchas refuse taps passed on this way, so the window on the PC stays the fallback. With "Stop early" (about a minute) the PC says which window Jarvis is stuck on, and the window is left exactly where it is unless you choose "Bring it to the front".

title: When the connection is catching up
what: Jarvis stops acting, and says so, rather than guessing.
where: The banner and the status line say it plainly.
asks: Nothing is decided while the stream is stale - refusing is never held, approving can be.
limit: This is deliberate: acting on a stale picture of the world is how the wrong thing gets approved.

title: Stop everything
what: Halts what Jarvis is doing on the screen or the phone, at once.
where: Press Alt+Shift+X on the PC. On the phone, the Stop button in Jarvis Live.
asks: It asks nothing first, and approves nothing.
limit: There is no control anywhere that clears a rush latch, and no approve-in-bulk.

title: Trust: content risk and the audit chain
what: Outside text that looked risky, and the chain that records what Jarvis decided.
where: Brain, Trust. The audit chain is on both apps (the phone draws it in Brain); the content-risk list is the desktop's.
asks: No card - it only reads.
limit: It holds what is waiting on you, so it can never be hidden. The full content-risk list is on the desktop only.

title: A warning when text tried to rush you
what: A banner saying outside text tried to hurry you into approving something.
where: The Brain, as the Rush latch banner.
asks: Nothing to press - it is a warning.
limit: No control clears it, and it is never hidden.

title: Jarvis marks what it read from outside
what: Once Jarvis has read an email, a page, a file or other outside text, it says so, and the turn is treated as tainted.
where: A line on the answer, and a line on the card that follows.
asks: It is what makes the next risky step ask: note writes, web searches, smart-home switches.
limit: Outside text is never learned as a fact, and the tier is raised when it tries to rush you.

title: Settings itself
what: The list of every switch and card, in both apps.
where: PC: the tray menu, Settings and help. Phone: Settings.
asks: No card.
limit: Always reachable - it can never be hidden.

title: Small Python scripts for sums and averages
what: The AI model can run a small Python script for maths or data work, in its own read-only sandbox.
where: PC: Settings, Data and maths sandbox. Phone: Settings, Data and maths sandbox.
asks: Turning the sandbox on asks first, with one approval card on the PC. Turning it off is instant. A run that reads a file you listed also asks first, showing the script and the file.
limit: It has no network, writes no file, reads only the listed files you picked, and refuses dangerous code before it starts. Its Windows job object blocks the clipboard, screen and desktop, but cannot block network access on its own.

title: Protected from Jarvis
what: A list of folders, files and programs Jarvis may not touch: blocked, or read-only meaning it may read but never act.
where: Settings, Protected from Jarvis - in both apps.
asks: Adding by hand on the PC is immediate because it only tightens. Adding by asking in chat raises one card, and removing an entry always raises one card.
limit: A program is matched by its executable name. The v1 gaps are named in the docs, section 171.5.

title: A short plan of several steps, one card
what: Propose a short plan of several steps and show the plan as one approval card before anything runs.
where: Ask for a plan; the plan card is one, then each risky step or result-filled step gets its own card before it runs.
asks: The plan itself is one card; a risky or result-filled step asks again on its own card.
limit: A plan is a proposal, never an action; it does not run by itself, and only steps the tools actually support are proposed.

title: A short card, then Explain more
what: Approval cards can open short with an Explain more button, or show everything at once; both apps read the same setting.
where: Settings, Approval cards; both apps read /api/card-prefs.
asks: No card to read or expand a card; the setting is stored on this PC.
limit: Only how much of a card is shown at first, not whether it asks or what it does. Start short is the default; Always full is the other choice.

title: A receipt for every change
what: Every action that changed something leaves a receipt with one Undo for that change.
where: No screen of its own: the receipts are routes only - GET /api/receipts for the list and POST /api/receipts/<receipt_id>/undo for Undo. The owner-facing Undo is the button on the action card; the Brain's separate Undo shelf is a different feature.
asks: No card to read a receipt; the action's own card has already happened, and Undo uses that receipt.
limit: Only actions that changed something; a read never makes one, and Undo lasts as long as the receipt's own window.
